title: microseris douglasii subsp. tenella
intro: Microseris douglasii subsp. tenella, commonly known as Douglas' silverpuffs, is a flowering plant species in the dandelion family. Douglas' silverpuffs have been traditionally used in herbal medicine for its purported health benefits, including anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties. The plant's therapeutic actions are thought to be due to its bioactive constituents, which include sesquiterpene lactones, phenolic acids, and flavonoids. The plant's bioactive constituents have been reported to exhibit anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial activities, suggesting potential therapeutic applications in the treatment of various diseases.
